findings.reason: a node implementing the verdict beside `tool_params()` in the embedded program leaves the rule in the parent image, so the reconnect the section exists to remove returns on the next rule change while the section reads as satisfied.
findings.text: "The child answers compatible or not, so a later change to the rule reaches running servers without a reconnect" does not follow from "the current code makes the compatibility decision": the child's probe reply, and any verdict composed beside it, is built in the probe handler of `SERVED_CHILD_PROGRAM` (`reckon/served_code.py:1362-1440`, probe reply at `:1433-1434`), a constant held by the running parent's own image and handed to the child at spawn (`reckon/served_code.py:1471`, `Popen([sys.executable, "-c", SERVED_CHILD_PROGRAM, str(root)])`), so a rule written there is the parent's frozen copy — exactly the defect `:306` blames `_probe_signature_changed` for; only a rule in the module the child imports from the checkout (`reckon/mcp.py`, imported by the child program at `reckon/served_code.py:1368`) reaches a server that is already running, and §13 names no such site.

findings.reason: without a case that fails when the rule sits in the parent's program string, the gate certifies a benefit the delivered code may not have.
findings.text: the child's-verdict case cannot falsify the wrong implementation: it needs a child whose rule the test controls, which is a stub child driven through the spawn hook the §11 gate already uses (`tests/test_a_slow_child_never_forces_a_reconnect.py:92-135`), so a stub answering "compatible" makes the parent serve whether the compatibility rule lives in the checkout or in the parent image's `SERVED_CHILD_PROGRAM`, and no case requires the verdict to come from checkout code.
